newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX power trades lower on cash, nuclear units.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX power trades lower on cash, nuclear units.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures were weaker Tuesday on bearish fundamentals as two California nuclear units boosted power, forecasts called for seasonable weather and lower physical power prices, sources said.
"Units are coming back, temperatures should cool off, and the cash really dumped this morning," said one Houston-based futures trader.

As of 1220 EDT, August Palo Verde (PV) was trading down $1.26 at $34.20 per megawatt hour (MWh) following exchanges in a range of $33.75-34.60, while September was down $1.21 at $27.35 after trades in a range of $27.00-27.95 per MWh.

August California Oregon Border (COB) was trading down 58 cents at $20.60 following exchanges in a range of $20.25-20.75 per MWh, while September COB was down 47 cents at $21.25 after trade at $21.00-21.70 per MWh.
NYMEX said as of 1145 EDT an estimated total of 630 PV and 312 COB contracts had traded.

Southern California Edison said Monday both the 1,070 megawatt (MW) San Onofre nuclear power unit 2 and the 1,080 MW San Onofre unit 3 were expected to return to full power before the end of the week.
The units, located in San Clemente, Calif., are returning from maintenance and refueling shutdowns.
In the physical markets, next-day peak PV power was said to be trading at near $29.00 Tuesday morning, down strongly from $36.00-41.00 per MWh on Monday for Tuesday delivery, sources said.
Meterologists called for seasonal summer temperatures across most of the West into next week.

Coastal cities from Seattle to Los Angeles were forecast to see readings in the 70s Fahrenheit, while interior centers in Southwest like Phoenix and Las Vegas were expected to hit the 100 degree mark later this week.
As of 1215 EDT, NYMEX Henry Hub natural gas futures were trading up 3.2 cents at $2.117 per million British thermal units.
